To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Thompson Sampling achieves an optimal prior-free regret bound, and it also achieves a prior-dependent regret bound that is uniformly bounded over time for a class of priors that includes the ones of Bubeck and Cesa-Bianchi [2007].
Thompson Sampling achieves optimal prior-free regret bounds and can also take advantage of nice properties of priors.

(i) Thompson Sampling has optimal prior-free regret bounds in the sense that it achieves the best possible regret for any prior distribution; (ii) Thompson Sampling is able to take advantage of the prior distribution in the sense that its performance can be much better than the best possible prior-free regret bound when the prior is well-chosen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the prior-dependent and prior-free regret bounds for Thompson sampling in the stochastic multi- armed bandit problem.
the following question: how much can a Bayesian regret be reduced by using a prior distribution?
the study of the prior-free and prior-depedent Bayesian regret bounds for the Thompson Sampling algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Thompson Sampling has a prior-dependent regret that can be arbitrarily small (and in fact uniformly bounded), and a prior-free regret that is bounded from above and below by constants.
for any prior, the regret of Thompson sampling is bounded by 14√K, and for the special case of the priors of Bubeck [2013], it is bounded by a constant.
Thompson Sampling is optimal for priors with bounded support, and that its performance is uniformly bounded for the setting of [Bubeck et al., 2013].
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for any prior, Thompson Sampling is optimal in a sense that is very close to the usual distribution-free setting, while for priors with nice properties it is optimal in a stronger sense.
the Bayesian regret of Thompson Sampling with respect to a prior distribution is bounded from above and below by functions of the form f(n)K, for some f(n) that depends only on n.
Thompson Sampling is a prior-dependent regret minimizer in the Bayesian setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Thompson Sampling is a good algorithm in the prior-free setting, and that it can greatly take advantage from the prior knowledge in some cases.
Thompson Sampling is not just a good algorithm for the Bayesian bandit setting, it is actually a good choice for any bandit problem with prior information on the reward distributions.
Thompson Sampling is a very flexible algorithm that is able to adapt very well to the prior distribution, even when the prior is far from the real distribution.
